misconceptions.description: Treating UDL as a retrofit only for students with formal accommodations
misconceptions.trigger: learner frames UDL as something added only after a complaint
misconceptions.feedback: UDL is proactive design for learner variability. It is meant to reduce barriers from the beginning, not just retrofit them later.

misconceptions.description: Separating accessibility from pedagogy as if it were only a compliance issue
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats accessibility checks as unrelated to learning design
misconceptions.feedback: Accessibility and pedagogy are intertwined. If learners cannot perceive, navigate, or respond in the environment, the instruction itself becomes unusable.

misconceptions.description: Assuming flexible representation or expression weakens academic standards
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues that offering multiple pathways automatically lowers rigor
misconceptions.feedback: UDL changes the path, not the standard. Learners can be held to the same objective while being allowed more than one valid route to access or express understanding.
